statement: On complete, saturated, phase-locked components, for h in the unsigned-incidence controller kernel (row-sum-preserving edge kernel) K = ker A_J the exact one-step multiplier is lambda = (1 - gamma*dt) s_J, under conditions (a) gate on, (b) clamp x >= 0 inactive, (c) R does not respond within the step, (d) delta below the untied gaps (no controller change), (e) equal controlling scales s_i = s_J on J. Under the further ideal hypotheses R = 1 and row sum c at the controlling nodes, lambda_k = (1 - gamma*dt) c / (c + dt(k*eta - gamma*c) + eps); kappa_k = k*eta/c - 1/T_w is its dt, eps -> 0 limit. Checked on 374 resolved components: 264 two-sided fibers (lambda to 2.1e-8 relative, kappa to 2.1e-6 absolute) and 110 all-tied K3s on one-sided controller-selection rays (lambda to 1.7e-7, kappa to 1.7e-5, 294 resolved rays). The observed ~2e-8 gap is unexplained (finite eps changes lambda by only ~1.6e-12; the audit says the gap is not isolated). Condition (c) holds automatically for a B-only perturbation: Engine v1 computes R from phase, history and EMA before B is updated, so a within-step R response is ruled out (ERRATA_2026-10-28.md E5). Remaining unverified candidates: finite-difference error, unequal controlling scales, finite-time departure from the ideal locked point, storage rounding. The maximum residual (2.04e-8) comes from a single component with a tiny finite-difference step (delta in [1e-9, 1e-8)); the other 263 well-resolved components agree within 2.1e-10, so finite-difference/rounding error is the most likely cause, and finite-time departure and unequal controlling scales are less likely. The gap stays unexplained until a step-size sweep is run.

statement: For an all-tied K_n (k = n - 1) with EQUAL EDGE WEIGHTS, the one-sided gate derivative has nonadditivity 1/sqrt(2k(k-1)) and odd defect sqrt(2/(k+1)); these ratios are derived, not empirical. They are not universal tied-clique formulas: for n >= 4 equal row sums do not imply equal edges, and an unequal-edge K4 (edge ratio 0.3 : 0.2 : 0.1, equal row sums) gives nonadditivity 0.2003 vs formula 0.2887 and odd defect 0.7254 vs 0.7071. The figures depend on which pair of adjacent edges is perturbed (other pairs: 0.2627 / 0.7254, 0.3046 / 0.7140), and the unequal-edge state is not a fixed point of the ideal gate (max one-step change 2e-4), so it refutes universality but is not a fixed-point counterexample. For K3, equal row sums force equal edges.
